wallbox.modbusNotConnected: The wallbox at {host} does not answer or accepts no Modbus connection. On EKD systems this is usually caused by the previous smartbox: as long as it has power, it holds the connection to the wallbox. Disconnect it from power, and OpenAmpere will read the wallbox again by itself. If that does not help, check the address and whether evcc or another program reads the wallbox.
wallbox.modbusNoAnswer: The wallbox accepts the connection but does not answer properly. On EKD systems this is usually caused by the previous smartbox: as long as it has power, it holds the connection to the wallbox. Disconnect it from power, and OpenAmpere will read the wallbox again by itself. If that does not help, maybe evcc reads the wallbox, or the unit ID is wrong.
wallbox.modbusBusy: The wallbox refuses to be read (“server device busy”). It probably does not allow Modbus in its current control mode. You can see the mode in the manufacturer's app.
wallbox.modbusRejected: The wallbox answers but does not know these registers. Maybe it is another model or another firmware.
wallbox.simulationReleased: {reason}, OpenAmpere would let go of the wallbox
wallbox.removedSwitchedOffOrChanged: wallbox removed, switched off or changed
wallbox.modbusWriteNotConnected: The wallbox at {host} does not accept a Modbus connection right now. On EKD systems the previous smartbox is usually the reason: cut it from power and try again.
wallbox.modbusWriteRejected: The wallbox did not accept the setting. It can probably only be controlled through its own app right now: in the “Fox Switch” app, set the connection type “Modbus TCP”.
wallbox.workModeNotSettable: OpenAmpere cannot set the work mode of this wallbox.
wallbox.workModeControlOff: Changes to devices are switched off. Set them to “Active” under Devices, then OpenAmpere can change the work mode of the wallbox.
wallbox.workModeNotTaken: The wallbox did not take the work mode. Maybe it does not allow this in its current control type.
wallbox.readBackFailed: The wallbox accepted the setting, but OpenAmpere could not read it back. Whether it applies you see after the next read of the wallbox.
wallbox.workModeNotAnswering: The wallbox does not answer right now. OpenAmpere can change its work mode only once it is reachable again.
wallbox.writeAnswerLost: The wallbox did not answer the setting. It may apply anyway: you see this after the next read of the wallbox.
wallbox.modbusWriteError: The wallbox refused the setting with an error (error number {code}). Try again in a few minutes. If it still fails, create a report under More → Diagnostics.
wallbox.fallbackNotTaken: The wallbox did not take the fallback current of 6 A. OpenAmpere therefore does not control it.
wallbox.workModeKeepControlled: Under real control the work mode must stay “Controlled”. Switch real control off first, then you can change it.
